tei:titleStmt.tei:title: אַחֵינוּ הַנְּתוּנִים בְּצָרָה וּבְשִׁבְיָה
Our brethren in distress and bondage, a plea for the safety of Am Yisrael at the conclusion of prayer and ceremonies by Seth (Avi) Kadish

tei:bibl.tei:title: אַחֵינוּ הַנְּתוּנִים בְּצָרָה וּבְשִׁבְיָה
Our brethren in distress and bondage, a plea for the safety of Am Yisrael at the conclusion of prayer and ceremonies by Seth (Avi) Kadish
tei:bibl.tei:author: Seth (Avi) Kadish
tei:bibl.tei:note: Converted from the export of opensiddur.org at 624215eef0.

tei:div.tei:p: This prayer is for all members of עם ישראל who are in danger or oppressed in our time: First and foremost for all Israeli soldiers, next for those who are in combat at this moment, then for captive or wounded soldiers and civilians alike, then “all those threatened by malice in our land and in exile” (mostly not soldiers), and finally “all those in need of Your comfort” which especially means the families of dead or wounded soldiers and civilians in Israel and in exile.

When I say this prayer in public at weddings (before the groom breaks the glass), I usually informally add “אחינו” to the first to groups: אחינו העומדים על משמר ארצנו and אחינו הלוחמים בשדה הקרב, because the soldiers defending our lives and defending the nation state of the People of Israel are indeed our brothers and our children.

I also usually add, regarding the wounded, ופצועים במערכה, חיילים ואזרחים, because the our enemies’ violence is directed at every member of the People of Israel, and to our sorrow it sometimes reaches them, whether they are soldiers defending life and liberty or civilians (both in Israel and abroud).
